No tool was invoked, so no data provider was contacted. ONE field is removed rather than stored: every tool's inputSchema carried a $schema URI naming the JSON Schema draft-07 dialect. It is dropped because storing it would put a host on this repository's allow-list that nothing else needs, and the dialect is a property of every draft-07 schema rather than a fact about this catalogue - API.md states it in words instead. Nothing else is altered: every tool, parameter, constraint, resource, template and prompt is as the server returned it. A SECOND substitution, for a different reason: two input schemas carried a 288-character regular expression validating an ISO-8601 date including leap years. Each is stored as patternLength rather than as its text, because such a regex spells its arithmetic as character classes of selected digits, and the leak sweep that guards this repository cannot tell a class of five digits from a five-digit internal value. The two ways to keep the text would both have been falsehoods - narrowing the sweep for every file, or an allow-list entry claiming a character class is a number this project publishes - so the text is not kept. Nothing about the constraint is hidden by this: API.md already summarised a pattern of over 60 characters by its length, which is what a reader gets either way, and the server hands anyone the full expression in tools/list.

serverInfo.name: viafrei
serverInfo.title: ViaFrei
serverInfo.description: The German Real-Time Mobility Context Platform for AI. ViaFrei gives AI assistants real-time awareness of Germany. Trains and buses, traffic and roadworks, fuel, charging, parking and weather. One MCP. No API key. No sign-up.

instructions: ViaFrei gives AI assistants real-time awareness of Germany: live motorway traffic, closures and roadworks (plus Land and city traffic messages where a feed carries them), fuel prices, EV charging, parking, train and public-transport departures, regional public-transport punctuality and service alerts, station lifts and escalators and DWD weather warnings; and, as reference data, places and addresses and the curated German driving rules. Every tool takes a `language` argument that defaults to German ("de"): set it on every call to the language the user writes in — "en" for English — or an English question is answered in German. Always show the attribution line of a result to the user, and when a result carries `_meta.purposeNote` or `_meta.conditionNote`, show that sentence verbatim as well — it is a legal condition of the data, not a caption. Times are Europe/Berlin; the rules answers carry a review date and are informational, not legal advice. ViaFrei is in beta: sources are still being added and answers and coverage can change, so when a decision depends on a closure, a departure or a price, tell the user to confirm it with the source the attribution line names.

tools.name: check_autobahn_traffic
tools.description: Per motorway (≤ 5): an Ampel verdict, then jams, closures and roadworks in force now, with delay/speed. Use when asked about a named motorway now: frei/clear (Ampel), Stau, a delay, how it looks, or a LIST of closures; name every motorway (Munich→Berlin: A9). Do NOT use for open/closed/gesperrt/passable, even now, a closure with no time word or a later one (tonight, weekend), or a town, no motorway — check_road_status; Baustellen dated or geplant — find_roadworks_ahead; a named city street: not held; fuel (find_cheapest_fuel), trains (get_train_departures). ~5 min old. Show attribution.

roads.description: Autobahn numbers, e.g. ["A9"] or ["A8", "A99", "A9"] (1–5 per call). Name every motorway on the route so the whole drive is briefed in one call — "A9", "A 9" and "a9" are the same road. Results are grouped per road, in the order you list them.

place.description: Optional: the town, junction or address the person is at or asks about ("A1 bei Köln", "A3 near Frankfurt"). Then each road's events within radius_km come first, nearest first, and the headline counts them with the road-wide total beside it. Omit it for the whole road. Give either place OR lat+lon, never both.

lat.description: Latitude in WGS 84, e.g. 48.137. Use with lon when the caller already holds coordinates; otherwise use place.

lon.description: Longitude in WGS 84, e.g. 11.576. Use with lat; otherwise use place.

radius_km.description: Radius around place or lat+lon in km (1–100, default 25). Ignored without a place.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

kinds.description: Which event kinds to return: warning = live traffic (jams, slow traffic, hazards), closure = full closures, roadworks = construction sites. Set it when the SUBJECT of the question is one of those categories by name: "Baustellen auf der A8?" is ["roadworks"], "welche Sperrungen sind in diesem Moment gemeldet?" is ["closure"]. Omit it when the question is how the road IS — Stau, frei, a delay, "wie sieht es aus", "everything"; the German "Stau?" is the idiom for the whole picture, and a filter nobody asked for hides the closure on the same stretch. Whether a closure question is this tool's at all is decided by two things, and the noun (Sperrung, Vollsperrung, closure) is neither. FIRST THE CLOCK: only a question about this minute (jetzt, gerade, in diesem Moment, right now, at this very minute) can be this tool's — with no time word at all, or for a later window (tonight, heute Abend, am Wochenende, the coming days), it is check_road_status. SECOND, WHAT IS ASKED, which the clock cannot see: what is REPORTED or in force on a named motorway is this tool ("which closures are in force on the A100 at this very minute?"), while whether the road is OPEN or passable is check_road_status AT ANY CLOCK — "ist die A8 offen", "ist die A3 in diesem Moment gesperrt?", "komme ich da durch?" — and so is a closure asked around a town instead of on a motorway number. Baustellen with a date or the word geplant are find_roadworks_ahead. Default: all three.

limit.description: Maximum events to return across all roads (1–50, default 10). Each road's most important item comes first, in the order you listed the roads, so every road with something in force is on the first page when limit is at least the number of roads; after that jams, then closures, other reports, then roadworks, the roads taking turns within each. Only what is in force now is listed — closures announced for later are counted apart in the headline.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous result's _meta.nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: find_cheapest_fuel
tools.description: Returns the cheapest stations for one fuel grade near a place or coordinate: price per litre, brand, address, distance, open state. Use when the user asks where to fill up or what fuel costs. Do NOT use for charging an electric car (call find_charging_station), price history, or traffic (call check_autobahn_traffic). Radius ≤ 25 km, at most 10 stations. For a brand, a name, open now or at a named time, or nearest-first, call find_fuel_station. Each line names the age of its price and opening-hours claim. Prices are consumer information only; the attribution line and MTS-K note must be shown.

place.description: Where to look, as free text: a city ("München", "Munich"), a district or Kreis ("Kreis Fulda"), a Bundesland, a station or stop ("Hamburg Hbf"), a motorway junction ("AK Neufahrn"), or a street address with a house number ("Bahnhofstraße 12, 36037 Fulda"). A motorway number alone ("A7") resolves to the road, which has no single point — name a town or junction on it instead. Use this instead of coordinates whenever the person named a place. An address needs its town or postcode — a street and a number alone exist in many towns. Give either place OR lat+lon, never both.

lat.description: Latitude in WGS 84, e.g. 48.137. Use with lon when the caller already holds coordinates; otherwise use place.

lon.description: Longitude in WGS 84, e.g. 11.576. Use with lat; otherwise use place.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

fuel.description: Fuel grade: "e5" (Super E5), "e10" (Super E10, the standard German petrol) or "diesel" — LPG/Autogas and CNG are not held by any source here: say so, never substitute a petrol grade. Default "e10". Pass the grade the person named — a diesel driver is not helped by a petrol price.

radius_km.description: Search radius around the place in kilometres (1–25, default 5). The provider's terms cap it at 25 km — a larger circle is a dataset request, not a consumer question.

limit.description: How many stations to return, cheapest first (1–10, default 5). The provider's terms cap it at 10.

tools.name: find_fuel_station
tools.description: Finds filling stations around a place or coordinate under any combination of filters — grade, brand, name, open now, open at a time you name, open 24 h — sorted by distance, price or name. Use when the question is WHICH station: the closest diesel to a stop, an ARAL open tonight, what one forecourt sells. Do NOT use for the plain "where is fuel cheapest" question (call find_cheapest_fuel) or for charging an electric car (call find_charging_station). Every result carries the attribution and the MTS-K note, and says how old each price and opening-hours claim is.

place.description: Where to look, as free text: a city ("München", "Munich"), a district or Kreis ("Kreis Fulda"), a Bundesland, a station or stop ("Hamburg Hbf"), a motorway junction ("AK Neufahrn"), or a street address with a house number ("Bahnhofstraße 12, 36037 Fulda"). Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

fuel.description: Only stations with a current price for this grade: "e5" (Super E5), "e10" (Super E10) or "diesel" — LPG/Autogas and CNG are not held by any source here, so say so rather than call for them. Omit to get every station near the place whatever it sells — the answer then lists all the grades it holds a price for. Required when sort is "price", because a price ordering needs a grade.

radius_km.description: Search radius around the place in kilometres (1–25, default 5). 25 km is the provider's own ceiling — a larger circle is a dataset request, not a consumer question.

brand.description: Only stations of this brand, matched case-insensitively anywhere in the brand field: "ARAL", "Shell", "TotalEnergies", "JET". Use it when the person named a chain ("die ARAL an der B1"). Free stations often carry no brand at all and are then not matched by any brand.

name.description: Part of the station's own name or brand, case-insensitive: "Autohof", "Raststätte Fulda". Use it when the person named a specific forecourt rather than a chain. Combine with place to keep the search local.

open_now.description: When true, only stations the published opening hours say are open at this moment. Default false. A station whose hours we have never read is NOT returned by this filter and is counted in the answer instead — the result never guesses that an unknown station is open.

open_at.description: Only stations open at that time in Germany (Europe/Berlin): "23:30" means the next time the clock shows 23:30, and "2026-09-30 06:15" a specific local date and time. Use it for "is it still open tonight". Do not pass it together with open_now — they ask the same question about two different clocks.

whole_day.description: When true, only stations the provider flags as open around the clock (24/7). Default false. Use it when asked whether a station never closes ("durchgehend geöffnet", "around the clock") and for a night drive; it is a stricter filter than open_now, which is satisfied by a station that closes at 22:00.

sort.description: Order of the answer: "distance" (nearest first, the default — use it for "closest diesel to Hamburg Hbf"), "price" (cheapest first, needs fuel), or "name" (alphabetical, for a person scanning a list of a brand's forecourts).

limit.description: How many stations to return (1–10, default 5).

tools.name: find_parking
tools.description: Parking near a place, a coordinate or along one motorway: lorry parks, car parks, P+R and disabled-badge bays, with total spaces, stated amenities (WC, shower) and published free spaces. Use when asked where to park or leave the car for the train ("Parkhaus in Köln", "Rastplatz A3", "P+R"). Do NOT use for fuel (find_cheapest_fuel) or EV charging (find_charging_station). Radius ≤ 25 km, ≤ 10 sites per list; ODbL and CC BY-SA sources are separate lists (up to three). No "free now" means no published count, not full. No prices: for "was kostet" say so, no call. Show each source's attribution.

place.description: Where to look, as free text: a city ("München", "Munich"), a district or Kreis ("Kreis Fulda"), a Bundesland, a station or stop ("Hamburg Hbf"), a motorway junction ("AK Neufahrn"), or a street address with a house number ("Bahnhofstraße 12, 36037 Fulda"). lon.description: Longitude in WGS 84, e.g. 11.576. Use with lat; otherwise use place.

Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

road.description: A single motorway number to list parking along, e.g. "A3" ("A 3" and "a3" are the same road). Use this when the person named a road and no town — "Rastplatz auf der A7". Give road OR place OR lat+lon, never two of them: a road is a 900 km line and a place is a point, so the two answer different questions. When the question names BOTH — "Parkhaus in Köln an der A3" — use the place: a person parks at a point, and the radius already covers the motorway beside it. A road list is in name order and cannot follow a direction of travel: for "A4 Richtung Görlitz" ask with place for the destination or the next town on the way instead, which answers nearest first.

kind.description: Which kind of parking: "car_park" = public car park (Parkhaus/Parkplatz), "park_and_ride" = P+R beside a station, "truck" = lorry parking, "any" = all of them. Default "any". "disabled_badge" = on-street bays reserved for a disabled parking permit (Behindertenparkplatz, Schwerbehindertenparkplatz), where a municipality publishes them, with a sensor's free/occupied where one is fitted — pass it only when such a bay was asked for; it is never part of "any" and takes place or lat+lon, not road. Rest areas are NOT a kind we can filter: no source we hold classifies them, so for "Rastanlage"/"Raststätte"/"rest area" leave kind out ("truck" when lorry spaces were asked for); "rest_area" is still accepted and answered as "any", with a sentence saying why. Pass a kind only when the person named one — a lorry driver asking for a break wants "truck", someone leaving the car for the train wants "park_and_ride". A camper, a caravan or a coach is none of these: leave the argument out rather than filtering a tourist into lorry bays.

radius_km.description: Search radius around place or lat+lon in kilometres (1–25, default 10). Ignored when you pass road, which covers the whole motorway. Start small in a city and widen if the answer is empty.

only_with_free_spaces.description: Set true only when the person asks whether spaces are free right now. It keeps just the facilities whose operator publishes live occupancy AND currently reports a space, and the result says how many were dropped for publishing nothing — most German parking publishes no occupancy at all, so true usually narrows the answer to very little. Default false.

facilities.description: Keep only sites whose own publisher states ALL of these amenities: "toilet", "shower", "restaurant", "snack", "cafe", "shop", "fuel", "charging", "drinking_water", "picnic", "playground", "wifi", "security", "accessible_toilet". Pass it only when the person asks for one — "Rastplatz mit Dusche an der A7" → road "A7", facilities ["shower"]; "car park with a toilet near Köln Hbf" → facilities ["toilet"]. Many publishers state no amenities, so the filter can narrow the answer to little; an amenity nobody stated is unknown, not absent, and the answer says how many sites state any. A toilet, restaurant or charger merely NEAR a site (listed beside it, from OpenStreetMap or the charging register) never satisfies the filter. Leave it out otherwise: every listed site already carries its amenity line.

limit.description: How many facilities to return, nearest first (1–10, default 5).

tools.name: check_road_status
tools.description: If a motorway/B/Land road (NI, NW, HE, BW, MV, SN, TH; B also SH, BY, BE; pass Land/town as place) is open/closed/restricted now/soon; by place, jams, city/Land messages, Hamburg traffic cameras; lorry limits, Lang-Lkw (vehicle). Use when asked if a road's open/closed/gesperrt/passable, even now — "A8 in diesem Moment gesperrt?" — closures tonight/weekend, or Stau in a town (Köln). Do NOT use for a named motorway frei/clear (Ampel) or its jams/delays — check_autobahn_traffic; dated roadworks — find_roadworks_ahead; a named city street: not held, no call. ≤14 days/11 entries. Show attribution.

road.description: One road: a German motorway, e.g. "A8"; a Bundesstraße in Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Hessen, Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Berlin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen or Thüringen, e.g. "B27"; or a Landes- or Staatsstraße in Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Hessen, Baden-Württemberg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen or Thüringen, e.g. "L1025" or "S296". "A8", "A 8" and "a8" are the same road. Use this whenever the person named a road — it is the only input that reaches the planned-works data, which is filed by road and section and carries no coordinates. When the person also says WHERE — a town or a Bundesland ("die B2 bei Potsdam", "L1025 in Niedersachsen") — pass that as place too: only sources for that Land answer, and a Land no source covers is named. L and S numbers repeat in every Land, so give the Land with them. Otherwise give exactly one of road, place, or lat+lon.

place.description: Where to look, as free text: a city ("München", "Munich"), a district or Kreis ("Kreis Fulda"), a Bundesland, a station or stop ("Hamburg Hbf"), a motorway junction ("AK Neufahrn"), or a street address with a house number ("Bahnhofstraße 12, 36037 Fulda"). An address needs its town or postcode — a street and a number alone exist in many towns. Give either place OR lat+lon, never both.

lat.description: Latitude in WGS 84, e.g. 48.137. Use with lon when the caller already holds coordinates; otherwise use place.

lon.description: Longitude in WGS 84, e.g. 11.576. Use with lat; otherwise use place.

horizon_days.description: Days ahead from now (0 = right now only, max 14, default 3). Only what was asked; count the days from today to the last day meant, both included: 0 for right now / jetzt / gerade; 1 for today, tonight, heute Abend; 2 for tomorrow; a weekday ("am Freitag") the days through it; "this weekend" the days through Sunday (Monday 7, Friday 3, Sunday 1); "next week" through next Sunday. A bare "is the A8 open?" asks for no window: omit it, never 0. Live closures, and by place the jams reported now, are always included.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (1–11, default 10). By road, closures come first, then restrictions in force, then planned works; by place, nearest first.

vehicle.description: Set ONLY when the person asks for a lorry (Lkw, truck, HGV) or a long lorry (Lang-Lkw, EuroCombi, Gigaliner): then the answer is where that vehicle may go, instead of closures. "long_lorry" with a road ("darf der Lang-Lkw auf die A7?") answers whether the road is in the long-lorry positive network; with a place, the network roads near it. "lorry" or "long_lorry" with a place ("Durchfahrtshöhe in Haan", "Lkw-Vorrangroute in Frankfurt", "Gewichtsgrenze in Bremen") answers the height, weight, width and lorry-ban signs near it, and the lorry priority routes, where a publisher holds them (NRW, Frankfurt RheinMain, Bremen). Omit for cars and for closures.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

tools.name: find_roadworks_ahead
tools.description: Returns roadworks PLANNED on one motorway, one Bundes-/Landesstraße in NI, NW, HE, BW, MV, SN or TH (BY: B only), or city streets by place, in a date window: section, restriction, dates. Use when a date or window is named, it says geplant, or how long a site lasts ("Baustellen auf der A7 in den Sommerferien?"). ONE road/place per call. Do NOT use when more than one motorway is named, for the situation this minute, or for Baustellen with neither date nor geplant — all three are check_autobahn_traffic; whether a road is open — check_road_status. ≤ 92 days, max 20 sites. Show attribution.

road.description: The road to look at, one per call: an Autobahn, e.g. "A7" or "A100"; a Bundesstraße in Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Hessen, Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen or Thüringen, e.g. "B6"; a Landesstraße in Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Hessen, Baden-Württemberg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern or Thüringen, e.g. "L1025"; or a Staatsstraße in Sachsen, e.g. "S296" — "A7", "A 7" and "a7" are the same road. B and L roads in other Länder and Kreisstraßen are not covered. Ask again for a second road. Give road OR place.

place.description: A place — a district, street or address, e.g. "Hamburg-Altona", "Berlin-Mitte", "Kiel" — for the city and Land roadworks held by point within 3 km of it. Where no such source covers the place, the answer says so. Give road OR place.

from.description: First day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD in German local time. Omit for today. Resolve relative wording ("next Friday", "in den Sommerferien", "nächsten Monat") into real dates yourself, counted from today's date; this argument never takes words, and it never takes a fixed example date — the window a person means moves with the calendar.

to.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for 7 days after `from`, which is the right window for "am I going to hit roadworks on this drive". The window may span at most 92 days. For "how long will this last" / "wie lange dauert die Baustelle noch", leave both dates out: the default 7 days already returns the site's planned end date. Only widen — 28 days is the sensible step — when the person asked about a period that long.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

limit.description: Maximum sites to return (1–20, default 10), ordered by planned start. Every returned site is in the structured result; the readable text prints the first 10 and says how many more of them are in the structured half. The answer always names how many sites the window holds in total, so a small limit never hides the size of the problem.

Use when an EV driver asks where to charge ("Wo kann ich laden?", "CCS 150 kW near Leipzig", "ist gerade eine Säule frei?"). Do NOT use for petrol or diesel — call find_cheapest_fuel; for E-Kennzeichen or Ladekarte rules — call get_driving_rules. Radius ≤ 25 km, ≤ 10 sites; availability is missing for most operators and is then unknown, never free. Show the attribution line.

An address needs its town or postcode — a street and a number alone exist in many towns. Give either place OR lat+lon, never both.

lon.description: Longitude in WGS 84, e.g. 11.576. Use with lat; otherwise use place.

Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

radius_km.description: Search radius around the place in kilometres (1–25, default 10). A charging stop is worth a detour, so this is wider than the fuel radius — but 25 km is the cap, and a larger circle is a dataset request rather than a driver's question.

connector.description: Plug the car needs: "ccs2" (CCS Combo 2 — the DC fast-charging standard on almost every European EV), "type2" (Typ 2 / Mennekes, the AC socket) or "chademo" (older Japanese DC, e.g. Nissan Leaf). Omit unless the person named their plug or their car model — filtering on a guess hides chargers they could have used.

min_power_kw.description: Only charging points of at least this many kW (1–1000). Use when the person names a number or asks for fast charging: 50 = DC fast (a bare "fast"/"schnell"/"Schnelllader"), 150 = HPC ("HPC", "ultra", "ultraschnell"), 300 = the fastest posts in Germany. Omit for "where can I charge" — 11 kW overnight is a valid answer to that question.

only_available.description: When true, return only sites with at least one point reported FREE right now. Default false. Use it when the person asks what is free at this moment. Note that only some operators publish live status: the result always says how many nearby sites were dropped because their status is unknown, so the filter never silently hides a charger that may well be free.

limit.description: How many lines to return, nearest first (1–10, default 5). Pass a value only when the person named the equipment itself ("Aufzug", "Rolltreppe", "lift", "escalator"): a question about a wheelchair, a pram, heavy luggage or step-free access keeps the default — an escalator carries a suitcase too, and a filter there hides half of what the traveller needs. Filtering does not change how a broken one is reported, only which ones are listed.

limit.description: How many facilities to list (1–50, default 20). Out-of-service equipment is listed first and the counts in the summary always cover ALL of them, so a shorter list never hides a broken lift.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

tools.name: watch_situation
tools.description: Opens a watch so THIS conversation is told when something changes: a road closed or restricted, a motorway jam, a stop running late, a weather warning, a charger freeing up. Use when asked to be told later: "sag mir Bescheid, wenn die A8 wieder frei ist", "tell me when a warning comes for Kiel". A name is enough as key; no lookup first. Do NOT use to look up now, nor for e-mail, SMS or alerts outside this chat — we cannot send one; say so. Set hours (≤ 24, default 3) for the time asked; condition narrows it (only the reopening, one charge point). Session-scoped, ≤ 10 watches. Show attribution.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

kind.description: What kind of thing to watch. `road` = one motorway or federal road (key: "A8", "B27") — reports a closure or restriction appearing or clearing, and on a motorway a jam (condition events) appearing or clearing; `station` = one public-transport stop (key: its name, "Köln Hbf", or its DHID) — reports departures running late past the threshold; `region` = a city, district or Land (key: its name, "Hamburg", or its AGS key, "14612") — reports the share of late trips crossing the threshold; `place` = a town or address (key: "Fulda") — reports road restrictions appearing within the radius, not a jam; `weather` = one DWD warn cell (key: a place name, "Kiel", or the cell id) — reports an official warning coming into force; `charger` = one charging site (key: a place, "Würzburg", or the site id) — reports a point turning free.

key.description: The thing to watch, in the person's own words — a name is enough and no read tool is needed first; the server resolves it and the answer names the key it resolved to. `road`: a road number ("A8", "B27"). `place`: a town or address ("Fulda"). `weather`: a place name ("Kiel"), resolved to the DWD warn cell it lies in — or a warn cell id ("801002000"); a Land or Kreis is an area and takes no single cell. `station`: a stop or station name ("Köln Hbf", "München, Marienplatz"), resolved to its DHID the way get_departures resolves a stop — or a DHID ("de:14612:28"); an EVA number from get_train_departures ("8000207") is not a DHID and is refused. `charger`: a place ("Würzburg"), resolved to the nearest charging site that reports live occupancy — or a site id from find_charging_station. `region`: a city, district or Land ("Hamburg", "Landkreis Fulda"), resolved to its AGS key the way check_transit_disruption resolves its region — or an AGS key ("14612"). A name that fits several places or stops gets a which-one list and opens no watch; call again with the chosen line.

request.description: The person's request in their own words ("sag mir Bescheid, wenn sich auf der A7 ein Stau bildet"). Pass it on every call: a jam asked for on a motorway is watched (the Autobahn GmbH's and the police's jam reports); on another road, and for a `place` watch, closures and restrictions only, never a jam or slow traffic, and the answer says so.

hours.description: How long to watch, in hours (default 3, maximum 24). Prefer this over `until`: it needs no knowledge of the current time. Give one of `hours` or `until`, never both.

until.description: An explicit end instant as ISO-8601 with an offset ("2026-09-20T18:40:00+02:00"), at most 24 hours ahead. Use only when the person named a time; otherwise use `hours`. Give one of `hours` or `until`, never both.

condition.description: Optional threshold; the keys of each kind, with an example: road {"event": "reopen"} (only the reopening), {"events": ["jams"]} (jams on a motorway); station {"delay_min": 20}; region {"late_share": 0.3, "delay_min": 5, "min_trips": 20}; place {"radius_km": 10}; weather {"min_level": 3}; charger {"point_id": "2"} (one charge point). Any other key, or a key of another kind, is refused by name; leave it out for the default. The answer repeats the condition it applies.

delay_min.description: station: minutes of delay that count as a disruption (default 10).

late_share.description: region: share of observed trips running late that trips the watch (default 0.25).

min_trips.description: region: below this many observed trips the share is noise (default 10).

radius_km.description: place: how far around the place to look (default 25).

min_level.description: weather: lowest DWD warning level worth reporting (default 2).

event.description: road: 'reopen' reports only a restriction (or jam) clearing; 'any' reports both (default).

events.description: road: what to report — 'restrictions' (closures, roadworks, restrictions; the default) and/or 'jams' (a jam the Autobahn GmbH or the police report on the motorway, motorways only). A jam watch: ["jams"]; both: ["restrictions", "jams"].

point_id.description: charger: one charge point of the site instead of any of them.

tools.name: stop_watch
tools.description: Ends a watch this conversation opened with watch_situation, so no further notifications arrive for it. Use when the person no longer needs to be told — "du musst mir nichts mehr zur A8 sagen", "stop watching that charger". No id at hand: pass kind ("weather") and key in the person's words ("A8", "Bamberg", "Kiel"); one match is stopped, several are listed. Do NOT use to look a situation up (call check_road_status), to list what is running (read viafrei://watches), or to cancel anything outside this chat. Another session's watch is never found. Results carry their attribution line.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

watch_id.description: The numeric id of the watch to stop, as `watch_situation` returned it (the 12 in viafrei://watch/12).

uri.description: The watch's resource uri, e.g. "viafrei://watch/12". Give either this or `watch_id`, not both.

kind.description: Instead of an id: the kind of watch the person means, as watch_situation took it ("road", "station", "region", "place", "weather", "charger"). "Turn off the charging alert" is kind "charger" alone.

key.description: Instead of an id: the watched subject in the person's words, as it was given to watch_situation — a road or place ("A8", "Bamberg"), and with `kind` a place for a weather or charger watch or a stop name for a station watch ("Kiel", "Köln Hbf"), which is resolved the way watch_situation resolved it. The id the watch carries works too. For a station, region, weather or charger watch a key that matches none of them falls back to `kind` alone. Matched against this session's open watches, case and spaces ignored. One match is stopped; several are listed and none is stopped.

prompts.name: plan_departure
prompts.title: Trip briefing before departure — Reise-Briefing vor der Abfahrt
prompts.description: Briefs a drive that is about to start: the official weather warnings at both ends, whether each motorway is open, and the jams in force this minute, ending in one go/no-go sentence. Use when the traveller asks whether to set off now, how the route looks today, or what is waiting on the A-roads. Do NOT use to weigh car against train — that is compare_travel_options; for a refuelling stop use plan_fuel_stop, for parking on arrival plan_arrival_parking. Show every result's attribution line.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.description: Where the drive starts, as the traveller wrote it. Example: "München" or "Bahnhofstraße 12, 36037 Fulda".

arguments.name: destination
arguments.description: Where the drive ends, as the traveller wrote it. Example: "Berlin".

arguments.name: roads
arguments.description: The motorways the route uses, comma-separated, at most five. Example: "A9, A4". Leave it out and the recipe names the obvious ones and says so.

arguments.name: departure
arguments.description: When the drive starts, in local words or as an ISO-8601 time with offset. Example: "now", "tomorrow 06:30", "2026-09-21T06:30+02:00". Defaults to now.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: compare_travel_options
prompts.title: Drive or take the train? — Auto oder Bahn?
prompts.description: Weighs one trip by car against the same trip by rail: closures and live jams on the motorway side, the next departures and the region's punctuality on the rail side, as two paragraphs the traveller can compare. Use when the traveller has not decided how to travel. Do NOT use once the decision is made — brief the drive with plan_departure, the rail leg with plan_commute. The punctuality figures keep their own attribution (share-alike unless VBB answered); show every attribution line.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.description: Where the trip starts, as the traveller wrote it. Example: "Köln".

arguments.name: destination
arguments.description: Where the trip ends, as the traveller wrote it. Example: "Frankfurt".

arguments.name: when
arguments.description: When they want to travel, in local words or as an ISO-8601 time with offset. Example: "this evening". Defaults to now.

arguments.name: roads
arguments.description: The motorways the drive would use, comma-separated, at most five. Example: "A3". Leave it out and the recipe names the obvious ones and says so.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: prepare_car_trip
prompts.title: What you need before driving in Germany — Vorbereitung der Autofahrt
prompts.description: Collects what a driver must carry and know before driving in Germany and into one particular city: the low-emission-zone badge, speed limits, winter tyres, the alcohol limit, tolls, mandatory equipment and the rules for an electric car. Use when the traveller is a visitor, is renting a car, or asks whether a city needs a sticker. Do NOT use for the live road situation — that is plan_departure — or for where to leave the car, which is plan_arrival_parking. Show the attribution and the review date.

arguments.name: destination_city
arguments.description: The city the driver will actually drive INTO, because the low-emission zone is a city rule. Example: "Stuttgart".

arguments.name: vehicle
arguments.description: What they are driving, when it changes the answer: "electric" adds the charging and badge rules, "lorry" the Sunday driving ban. Defaults to a petrol or diesel car.

arguments.name: topic
arguments.description: One rule topic, if they asked about exactly one — the same nine values get_driving_rules takes. Map what they said: Umweltplakette/Feinstaubplakette/low-emission zone → "lez", Winterreifen → "winter", Tempolimit → "speed", Promillegrenze → "alcohol", Maut → "toll", Sonntagsfahrverbot → "truck_ban", Warnweste/Verbandkasten → "equipment", Rettungsgasse/Panne → "emergency", E-Auto/Laden → "ev". Leave it out for the overview of all nine.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: plan_fuel_stop
prompts.title: Refuel or charge on the way — Tank- oder Ladestopp unterwegs
prompts.description: Finds where this traveller fills up or charges on the way: the cheapest stations for one fuel grade around one place, or the charging points with the right connector and power, and the rest area beside them if they also need a break. Use when the tank or the battery is the question. Do NOT use to brief the whole route — that is plan_departure — and not for parking at the destination, which is plan_arrival_parking. Prices are consumer information for this traveller alone; show every attribution line and any purpose note verbatim.

arguments.name: place
arguments.description: Where the traveller will be when they need the stop — a town, a junction, a station or a street address with its postcode. One place per call. Example: "Ingolstadt" or "A9 Anschlussstelle Allershausen".

arguments.name: energy
arguments.description: What the vehicle takes. "electric" switches the recipe to charging points; the three fuel grades go to the fuel stations. Set it whenever they named a grade — the fallback is "e10", the standard German petrol and find_cheapest_fuel's own default, and the recipe then says out loud that it was assumed.

arguments.name: radius_km
arguments.description: How far they are willing to detour, in kilometres, at most 25 (the provider's limit). Example: "10". Defaults to 5.

arguments.name: break_too
arguments.description: "yes" if they also want somewhere to stop and rest, which adds one parking call on the same road. Defaults to "no".

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: plan_commute
prompts.title: Plan today's commute by train — Pendelfahrt für heute planen
prompts.description: Plans one public-transport leg on the day itself: the next departures from the station with delays, platforms and cancellations, and whether the region's buses and trains are running normally at this hour. Use when the train is already the decision — a daily commute, or any leg where they need the next departures and nothing else. Do NOT use to weigh rail against driving — that is compare_travel_options — and not for motorway traffic, which is plan_departure. The punctuality figures (share-alike unless VBB answered) stay in their own paragraph; show every attribution line.

arguments.name: from_station
arguments.description: The station they leave from, as they say it. Example: "Köln Hbf", "Munich Central".

arguments.name: to_station
arguments.description: Where they are heading, used only to pick the right departures out of the board. Example: "Düsseldorf". We hold no journey planner, so this never becomes a route.

arguments.name: when
arguments.description: When they want to leave, in local words or as an ISO-8601 time with offset. Example: "in 20 minutes". Defaults to now.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: plan_arrival_parking
prompts.title: Where to leave the car on arrival — Parken am Ziel
prompts.description: Finds where to leave the car at the end of the drive: the car park in town, the park-and-ride at the edge with the onward departures, or the rest area if the traveller is early. Use when the drive is ending, or whenever someone asks where to put the car. Do NOT use for a refuelling or charging stop — that is plan_fuel_stop — and not for the live road situation, which is plan_departure. A facility that publishes no occupancy is reported as such, never as zero free spaces; show every attribution line.

arguments.name: destination
arguments.description: Where they want to park — a town, a district, a station or a street address with its postcode. Example: "Köln Innenstadt", "Freiburg Hbf".

arguments.name: kind
arguments.description: Which kind of parking: "car_park" is the enclosed Parkhaus in town, "park_and_ride" the P+R at the edge, "rest_area" the Rastanlage beside a motorway, "truck" a lorry site. Defaults to "any".

arguments.name: arrival
arguments.description: When they arrive, in local words or as an ISO-8601 time with offset. Example: "in 40 minutes". Defaults to now.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: find_a_place
prompts.title: Find out what a name refers to — Herausfinden, was ein Name meint
prompts.description: Resolves a bare name of unknown kind into a place, a named thing, or an address, trying each table in turn and stopping at the first that answers. Use when the traveller names something and you do not yet know whether it is a town, a company, or a street address — or to recover after a tool reported a name as ambiguous. Do NOT use once the kind is already known: a settlement name goes straight to find_place, a company or landmark to find_poi, a street address to find_address. Show every attribution line.

arguments.name: query
arguments.description: The name to resolve, exactly as the traveller wrote it. Example: "Neustadt", "adesso", "Bahnhofstraße 12, 36037 Fulda".

arguments.name: near
arguments.description: A second place to measure from, used only if find_place answers with more than one candidate for a common name. Example: "Hamburg".

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: plan_local_errand
prompts.title: What is around this place? — Was ist hier in der Nähe?
prompts.description: Answers "what is around here" for one place: the nearest fuel, EV charging, parking, railway station and motorway junction in one glance, then — only if the traveller wants more than the nearest one — the depth tool for that one category. Use when it is a quick local stop with nothing decided yet. Do NOT use once the traveller already knows what they need: a fuel grade's price is plan_fuel_stop or find_cheapest_fuel directly, a specific connector or live status is find_charging_station, parking kind or occupancy is find_parking. Show every attribution line.

arguments.name: place
arguments.description: Where the errand happens — a town, junction, station or street address with its postcode. Example: "Fulda".

arguments.name: need
arguments.description: Narrow the glance to one category when the traveller named one. Defaults to "everything", the full glance across all five categories find_nearby covers.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.

prompts.name: explain_this_coordinate
prompts.title: Say where a coordinate is — Sagen, wo eine Koordinate liegt
prompts.description: Turns a bare lat/lon into a sentence a traveller understands: the nearest address, settlement and motorway junction with their distances, and the Gemeinde, Kreis and Land the point lies in. Use whenever you already hold a coordinate — from the traveller, or from another tool's result — and need to say where it is. Do NOT use to look a place up BY NAME: that is find_a_place, find_place, find_poi or find_address. The Gemeinde, Kreis and Land are read off the municipality's official key (#683), not the nearest gazetteer point. OpenStreetMap ODbL 1.0 for the address; show the attribution line.

arguments.name: lat
arguments.description: Latitude of the point, as a decimal degree. Example: "50.5546".

arguments.name: lon
arguments.description: Longitude of the point, as a decimal degree. Example: "9.6773".

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Set this to the language the traveller is writing in: "en" for English, "de" for German. It decides both the language you answer in and the language argument you pass to every tool call in the recipe. Leave it out only when the language is genuinely unclear — the fallback is German, because the road is German.
